unit.why: A short anecdote: on a Friday night R. Baruch of Medzhybizh pauses while reciting Ribbono shel Olam, asks himself a question, answers it and weeps; R. Moshe of Savran overhears him and asks why he wept.

stories.start_quote: פ״א בליל ש״ק הלך על פני הבית
stories.summary_en: While reciting Ribbono shel Olam on Friday night, R. Baruch of Medzhybizh asks himself why he should thank God now for future kindness, answers that later he may not be in the right spiritual state to give thanks, and weeps; R. Moshe of Savran overhears him and asks him why he wept.

tags.why: The story is set on Friday night.

quotes: ואמר שלום עליכם ורבון העולמים כדרכו
מודה אני לפניך ה׳ אלהי וכו׳
tags.why: He is reciting the Sabbath-eve liturgy.

quotes: בכיתי מדוע לא אהיה אז בבחו׳ הראוי
tags.why: He weeps out of spiritual grief that he may later fall from his level.

quotes: אולי לא אהיה אז בבחינה זו להודות לך כראוי
tags.why: He doubts his own future spiritual worthiness.

quotes: והה״ק ר׳ משה מסאווראן עמד אז בקרן זוית
tags.why: R. Moshe of Savran overhears him and questions him.
The anecdote illustrates the tzaddik's piety in giving thanks.

quotes: ושאל לעצמו למה לי להודות לך על חסד העתיד
tags.why: His question and answer work as a short exegesis of the prayer text.
